I even tried uninstalling and reinstalling the app, but nothing fixed the problem. I was able to finish the series, but it was a struggle. I had paid for a yearly subscription, and when I requested a refund through Apple, it was denied. I wish the app worked more consistently, because I did enjoy the content, but the technical issues really took away from the experience.

If the developer could get me a refund that would be greatly appreciated.

reviews.title: Wait or pay
reviews.text: I think these short stories are actually good unlike a lot of the rest of the halfway AI generated stuff you see as ad’s on your social media platforms. The problem isn’t the stories, it’s the greedy attempts to get an unnecessary amount of money out of its viewers. The initial story will let you get 15/40 episodes in before it asks you for a payment of some sort to continue the story, which is typical for apps like these…however, if you don’t pay you wait 19 hours to unlock the next episode, WHICH IS ONLY 50 SECONDS LONG OR SHORTER. That wouldn’t even be a problem if you had to wait 19 hours to unlock around 5-10 more episodes but you only get 1 episode out of the long wait OR you pay $20 a month for a subscription to the story. $20 a month for 50 second episodes that only have 40 episodes total is absolutely not worth it, try $5 and maybe you’d actually have a lot more subscribers because the stories ARE GOOD ENOUGH to pay a little bit of money to watch them, it’s the same concept of Netflix but Netflix charges for access to movies, tv shows, interactive games, and more. Like I said, I’d pay $5.99 give or take for the SHORT stories to let me actually watch them all the way through without be interrupted every 30-50 seconds demanding an obnoxious amount of money for me…also the actors in these shorts deserve to have their work put out there for people to see, not just who can afford to see.

reviews.title: Good stories… a bit misleading in the app description
reviews.text:
This App should include a disclaimer: “Great stories you’ll love and must pay to watch”. 
They really should tell you before you download the app that after the first 5ish free chapters, you have to pay for each one if you want to watch the rest. There’s no “watch ads” or games or anything to earn/collect coins to unlock episodes. You get 1 free 30 second episode every 24 hours, and there’s no way to get the 50 coins to unlock the next one unless you “top up” by buying one of their coin packages or a subscription.
I gave 2Stars because the story’s are good and addictive, you can sign in to save progress, and they do a nice jobs with the recommendations for you. 
However, if you decide to download… be prepared to pay.

reviews.title: Buggy compared to other apps, but great with original selections
reviews.text:
I don’t know if it’s just a me issue, but every time I’ve used the app so far, I am unable to unlock episodes that I did actually wait out. Some of my other general complaints:
- no ability to save series to a designated library like you would on similar apps or even on Galatea.
- position seems to save at the last free-unlocked episode, which is tedious even when you’re just two episodes past that
- can’t change the playback speed on episodes to help make them go faster. Not a huge deal, but minorly annoying as someone who is neurodivergent and utilizes that feature often.

Compliments:
- the selection is FANTASTIC. Well-edited, original stories (usually originating from Galatea, making it really good for drawing traffic between both apps) with actors who seem to know what they’re doing, and even though the tropes are there, they’re disguised better than other apps.
- the app is pretty easy to navigate and coins don’t seem to be hard to get (according to other reviewers, which is believable based on how easy they are to get on Galatea as well)
- guaranteed actual free episodes of you wait out the countdown. No “watch __ ads to unlock __ episodes” that ultimately last longer than the episode themselves like I find on other apps.

reviews.text: Honestly laughable. I uninstalled the day I got it. Unless you want to pay $70/year or $20/week for a membership, you have to wait until a new episode/clip unlocks. It let me watch about 10 minutes of a show, then locked and I had to wait 90 mins for the next clip to unlock. The next clip was only 90 seconds and then locked again and said I had to wait 12 hours before the next clip would unlock. The fact an app thinks I’ll wait 12 hours for a 2 minute clip to unlock and then do it all over again is laughable. Waste of my time.

reviews.title: Suspicious Payment Options
reviews.text: Why is it that if I want to buy ‘coins’, I can do it directly with my Apple account, but if I try to buy the $20 a week you take me to an external website that asks for my credit card number? I get that Apple takes a cut when the payment goes through them, but you don’t mind them taking a cut when people buy ‘coins’. Why aren’t you letting people pay through Apple? This feels like a ploy to get credit card numbers and make it impossible to cancel the subscription like many people are saying in other reviews. I’m fine with paying for the week, but I’m not giving your app my credit card number.
